text: Program Description Teaching Objective The aim of international politics program is cultivate international politic specialists who proficient in basic theory of international politics, world economics, and economic diplomacy. The graduates should understand the world situation changes and the international economic and trade status; skilled in diplomatic negotiation, and able to business negotiation, communication and exchanges Why Choose to Study This Program The department of international politics has taken a great number of national, provincial, and 211 research projects in the field of national soft power, regional political and economic cooperation, overseas interest protection, international immigration and international security. The department also published and issued a batch of scientific research paper, which make the department has its place in academic area. Main Courses and credits Compulsory Courses Credits Elective Courses Credits Principles of Political Science 3 Political Economy of European Union 2 Introduction to International Relations 3 Political Economy of United States 2 International Institutions and Organizations 3 Political Economy of Japan 2 International Political Economics 3 Political Economy of Developing Countries 2 Chinese Foreign Strategy and Diplomacy 3 Enterprises and Market in China 2 Chinese Political Economics 3 China's Foreign Economic Relations 2 Chinese Politics and History 3 Political Economics of Energy and Environment 2 Political Economics of Transition 3 The Political Economy of Immigrations 2 Public Leadership and Public Policy 3 Modern Diplomacy 2 Foundations of International Laws 3 Public Diplomacy 2 International Conflict and Crisis Management 3 International Strategies 2 Dissertation Seminar 3 Globalization and Global Governance 2 International Negotiations 2 International Development 2 Mao Zedong Thought and Deng Xiaoping Theory 2 Internship & Career Steigenberger Group- Hotel Management Dentsubfc-PR SwissCham Beijing- Projects Assistant & Communication Assistant Thesis (4 Credits) In the fourth year of their study, students must complete a thesis related to their major to meet the graduation requirements. The length of the thesis should be around 8000 words. The thesis is a milestone assessment on the intended level of achievement both in the major and the general learning outcomes by the students. Specifically, students, must demonstrate the ability to apply their learning to complex, unscripted problems in the context of their advanced studies, the mastery of the skills required for their disciplines as well as essential learning outcomes including the breadth and the depth of their knowledge, critical and creative thinking, problem solving, the ability to integrate knowledge and skills and present their work in an appropriate manner.
